name: ISL3178EIBZ-T
title: ISL3170E to ISL3178E: ±15 kV ESD protected 3.3 V full fail-safe RS-485/RS-422 transceivers, 250 kbps, 500 kbps or 20 Mbps
summary: A family of nine single RS-485/RS-422 transceivers for a 3.3 V supply, with bus pins protected to ±15 kV IEC61000-4-2 and a 1/8 unit load receiver that lets 256 nodes share one bus. Receivers are full fail-safe; drivers are current limited with thermal shutdown. Versions differ by data rate (250 kbps or 500 kbps slew limited, or 20 Mbps), full or half duplex, and whether DE/RE enables, hot plug and shutdown are present. ISL3178EIBZ-T is the 20 Mbps half-duplex part with enables in 8 Ld SOIC, on a 2,500-piece reel.
key_figures: 250 kbps, 500 kbps or 20 Mbps min by version (ISL3178E: 20 Mbps)

notes: All parts are Pb-free (RoHS compliant), with a matte tin plus anneal (e3) lead finish that suits both SnPb and Pb-free soldering; the MSL rating is set at Pb-free peak reflow temperatures to IPC/JEDEC J STD-020.
On the SOIC 8 parts the marking is two lines: the device number over EIBZ.
Reel details are in Renesas TB347; MSL details in TB363.

circuits.title: Typical operating circuit, half duplex (ISL3172E, ISL3175E, ISL3178E)
circuits.description: Two half-duplex transceivers share one twisted pair. Each node runs from +3.3 V with a 0.1 µF capacitor from VCC to ground, and its A/Y and B/Z pins land on the pair. The pair carries an RT across its two wires at each end. Each node's RO, RE, DE and DI go to its own controller; DE and RE choose whether that node talks or listens.

Each pair has one RT across it, at its receiving end. Each node has +3.3 V with a 0.1 µF capacitor from VCC to ground. DI and RO of each node go to its controller.

circuits.title: Typical operating circuit, full duplex, 14 Ld SOIC (ISL3170E, ISL3173E, ISL3176E)
circuits.description: The full-duplex link with enables: two transceivers on two twisted pairs, each driver feeding the far node's receiver, with one RT across each pair at the receiving end. Each node has +3.3 V on pin 14 with a 0.1 µF capacitor to ground, and both GND pins to ground. RO, RE, DE and DI of each node go to its controller. Pin numbers are for the 14 Ld SOIC.
notes: GND is pins 6 and 7 together; NC is pins 1, 8 and 13, left open.
The ISL3170E and ISL3173E use the same pins.

operation.text: Nine 3.3 V RS-485/RS-422 transceivers that differ in three things: driver speed (ISL3170E-72E slew limited to 250 kbps, ISL3173E-75E slew limited to 500 kbps, ISL3176E-78E unlimited for 20 Mbps), pinout (full duplex with separate driver and receiver pins, or half duplex with the two sharing A/Y and B/Z), and whether the part has DE and RE enables. The ISL3171E, ISL3174E and ISL3177E are full duplex in 8 leads with neither enable and have no hot plug or shutdown. The ISL3178E is the 20 Mbps half-duplex part with enables, in 8 Ld SOIC or MSOP.

Each receiver input is at least 96 kΩ, eight times the 12 kΩ that defines one RS-485 unit load, so a part is 1/8 unit load and 256 of them can share one bus inside the standard's 32-unit-load limit without repeaters. Bus pin currents are +125 µA / -100 µA at most.

Both standards carry data differentially. RS-422 allows one driver and up to 10 one-unit-load receivers per bus; RS-485 allows 32 unit loads of drivers and receivers in any mix, and requires drivers to survive bus contention. The bus pins work over the -7 V to +12 V common-mode range, needed for runs up to 4000 ft where ground offsets and induced voltages appear.

The differential receiver is more sensitive than ±200 mV. Its upper threshold sits at -50 mV, so 0 V between A and B reads as a high: the output is high with the inputs open, shorted together, or terminated with no driver active (full fail-safe). Inputs work with common-mode voltages from -7 V to +12 V. On every version except the ISL3171E, ISL3174E and ISL3177E, RE low enables RO and RE high puts it in high impedance. The slew-limited versions (ISL3170E-75E) also filter the receiver input for noise immunity with slow input edges.

The driver gives at least 1.5 V across 54 Ω (RS-485) and at least 2 V across 100 Ω (RS-422), with low skew between its outputs. DE high enables it and DE low puts Y and Z in high impedance, except on the ISL3171E, ISL3174E and ISL3177E. The 250 kbps and 500 kbps drivers have limited output slew rate to cut EMI and reflections from unterminated or poorly terminated lines and stubs; the ISL3176E-78E drivers are not limited and run at 20 Mbps or more.

On the versions with enable pins, a circuit watching VCC keeps the driver and receiver outputs disabled for a while at power-up whatever DE and RE are doing, so a controller that has not yet set its control lines cannot make the driver fight a live bus.

Every pin has Class 3 HBM protection (above 7 kV). The bus pins carry stronger structures rated ±15 kV HBM, ±15 kV IEC61000-4-2 air gap and ±8 kV IEC61000-4-2 contact, working powered or unpowered and without narrowing the -7 V to +12 V common-mode range. The IEC test is made on the part powered in its typical circuit; the bus pins meet Level 4 with no extra protection on the board, so no transient suppressors and their capacitance are needed.

Short-circuit current limiting keeps the driver output current inside the RS-485 limit across the whole common-mode range, and a foldback circuit lowers the current further whenever the contending voltage is beyond either supply. If the die gets too hot, thermal shutdown turns the drivers off and turns them back on after the die has cooled by about 15 °C; under a lasting fault this cycles until the fault clears. The receivers keep working during thermal shutdown.

Versions with shutdown enter it when the receiver and driver are both disabled (RE = VCC, DE = GND) for 600 ns or longer, and supply current falls to about 10 nA. Both disabled for under 50 ns never causes shutdown. Coming out of shutdown, enable times are longer: tZH(SHDN) and tZL(SHDN) in the switching tables.

Achievable data rate falls as the network gets longer: the 20 Mbps parts are limited to under 100 ft, while the 250 kbps parts run at full rate over several thousand feet. Twisted pair is the cable to use; the receivers reject the noise it picks up as common mode. The 20 Mbps parts need proper termination; short networks with the 250 kbps parts can go unterminated, though termination is advised unless power is the main concern. With a single driver, put a terminator equal to the cable's characteristic impedance (typically 120 Ω) at the far end of the main cable from that driver; with several drivers, terminate both ends. Keep stubs to the main cable short.
If the receiver enable is not needed, RE goes to GND, directly or through 1 kΩ to 3 kΩ. If the driver enable is not needed, DE goes to VCC through 1 kΩ to 3 kΩ.
DE and RE draw current once they are more than 500 mV above VCC, limited by an internal 340 Ω resistor (about 13 mA at VIN = 5 V with VCC = 0 V). Short periods with VCC ≤ VIN ≤ 7 V do no damage.
